name: Robert Bigelow

summary.text: Robert Bigelow is a Las Vegas real-estate developer who owns the extended-stay chain Budget Suites of America and founded Bigelow Aerospace. In 1995 he founded the National Institute for Discovery Science, which studied reports at a Utah property known as Skinwalker Ranch that Bigelow acquired in 1996. He is a long-time friend of former Senator Harry Reid, who has said Bigelow helped frame the study that became the DIA's AAWSAP program, most of whose funds went to Bigelow's company. He is a major political donor, ranked 22nd among individual federal contributors in the 2022 cycle by OpenSecrets.

facts.claim: Bigelow owns Budget Suites of America, an extended-stay apartment chain, and is the founder of Bigelow Aerospace. Forbes reported that, starting with a $20,000 loan, he built roughly 15,000 rental units and bought about 8,000 more over his career.
facts.quote: starting with a $20,000 loan, Bigelow began investing and then building rental apartment complexes

facts.claim: Bigelow founded the National Institute for Discovery Science (NIDS) in 1995; the institute was disbanded in 2004. He acquired a cattle ranch in Utah known as Skinwalker Ranch in the mid-1990s, described by Forbes as a 480-acre property.
facts.quote: Bigelow founded the National Institute for Discovery Science in 1995, and the institute was disbanded in 2004.

sources.title: Robert Bigelow and the Bigelow Institute for Consciousness Studies

facts.claim: Harry Reid said that Bigelow knew of his interest in the subject and, when Reid asked for advice on how to approach Senate spending, offered to prepare a study framework, saying he would 'prepare something for you that anyone can look at it that wants to, it's strictly science.' Most of the resulting program's money went to Bigelow's aerospace company, which was the contractor.
facts.quote: prepare something for you that anyone can look at it that wants to, it's strictly science

facts.claim: The Associated Press and Las Vegas Sun reported that Bigelow convinced his friend, then-Senator Harry Reid, to allocate $22 million to the program later known as the Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program, and that much of the money went to Bigelow's company. Bigelow said he considered Reid a good friend and that late in Reid's Senate tenure they maintained the friendship by not talking politics.
facts.quote: Bigelow said he considered Reid a good friend, though toward the end of Reid's tenure in the Senate, they maintained that friendship by not talking politics.

facts.claim: The Las Vegas Sun reported that Bigelow donated at least $47 million in the 2022 midterm cycle, mostly to Republican causes, including roughly $25 million to Nevada gubernatorial nominee Joe Lombardo and $10 million to the PAC Friends of Ron DeSantis; OpenSecrets ranked him 22nd among top individual federal contributors that cycle.
facts.quote: Bigelow donated at least $47 million during the midterm elections campaign cycle to mostly Republican causes

sources.title: Nevada billionaire Bigelow opens his wallet

facts.claim: According to a Federal Election Commission filing reported by the Las Vegas Sun, Bigelow made a single contribution of more than $20 million in 2023 to Never Back Down, the super PAC supporting Ron DeSantis.
facts.quote: He also made a single contribution worth more than $20 million to the super PAC known as Never Back Down, according to a Federal Election Commission filing.

sources.title: Las Vegas billionaire Bigelow gives $20M to DeSantis super PAC

openQuestions: No record was found of Bigelow contributing to Harry Reid's own campaigns or leadership PACs; the page's 'political mega-donor' link to Reid specifically needs FEC/OpenSecrets confirmation (his documented large gifts are to Republican candidates and PACs).
The ranch purchase price and acreage differ by source (512 acres for $200,000 vs. 480 acres), and the reported 2016 sale to Brandon Fugal for about $4 million was not pinned to a citable source here.
